### What does this PR do?

When FSDP score centering processes a recorded sampler head, the head-scoring helper and sampled-token CE currently normalize the same vocabulary separately. This follow-up shares head/sample normalization and computes complete-support loss scores directly in the verified support. Unknown/incomplete rows keep the existing recorded-top-k plus full-vocabulary trainer-tail approximation, including its epsilon regularization. Sampling and recording parameters do not change.

Dependency: the automatic alignment and coverage-receipt changes in #8196. This draft is stacked on codex/sc-auto-support-8196, a mirror of the reviewed #8196 feature head; its diff contains only the two performance commits. It will be retargeted/rebased onto main after #8196 merges. This adds a separate full-local-vocabulary FSDP path. #8199 remains the Megatron/TP extension and can continue to use the unchanged general correction-helper APIs. #8020 proposes broader support replay for IS/RS and is outside this optimization.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Checked #8020 and open references to #8010/#8020; [open centering PR search](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+centering) found #8196 and #8199. Neither implements shared FSDP head/sample normalization. This PR depends on #8196 and does not reimplement its feature scope.
- [x] Title uses the repository's module/type format.

### Test

Commands run with the existing uv environment from the performance checkout:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 uv run --active --no-sync pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_shared_scores_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_score_centering_shared_engine_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_score_centering_wiring_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_on_cpu.py
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --active --no-sync pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/test_score_centering_shared_scores_on_gpu.py
uv run --active --no-sync pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure
```

Results: **89 CPU tests passed, 30 CUDA/Triton tests passed, all 14 pre-commit hooks passed**. CUDA tests cover no IS/TIS/IcePop, FP32/BF16, mixed alignment, noncontiguous logits/receipts, sampled/head collisions, entropy/KL consumers and unchanged input logits. Six CPU and six CUDA cases additionally check low-entropy supports with large common logit offsets against an independent FP64 expected-score objective. An independent scorer check passed 18 additional CUDA cases, with max FP32 gradient error 2.98e-8 and no BF16 error on those fixtures.

Additional bounded integration artifacts include 20 tiny-Qwen2 CUDA gates (8 actual model parameter-gradient comparisons, dense/packed B2 with lengths [8,5]) and 4 SP2 gates with actual NCCL/Ulysses gather, 13-to-14 padding and unpadding. These use the actual engine/loss hooks but do not exercise FSDP wrapping or distributed attention. SP2 candidate versus matched legacy-SP parameter-gradient relative L2 was 1.29e-7–1.46e-7 for FP32 and 0.350%–0.373% for BF16. BF16 is not bitwise equivalent because sparse contributions are accumulated in FP32 before a single cast.

Matched loss-pipeline benchmark: H100 80GB, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, BF16, N=4096, V=151936, K=128, 4 warm-ups and 6 ABBA rounds (12 observations per route). The baseline is the #8196 automatic correction helper plus sampled CE; both routes retain identical mass/alignment/tail diagnostics.

| Verified aligned rows | Baseline median ms | Shared median ms | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% | 21.100 | 8.908 | 57.8% |
| 50% | 21.103 | 8.705 | 58.7% |
| 100% | 21.103 | 8.421 | 60.1% |

Peak allocated memory, including identical inputs: 6,236,165,120 -> 3,749,990,400 bytes (5.808 -> 3.492 GiB). Max fixture loss difference 4.47e-8, BF16 logits-gradient max difference 7.63e-6, mass-metric max difference 4.17e-7. The repository benchmark script reproduces the fixture and records source SHA, environment and measurement scope.

This measures synthetic-logits score/loss forward and dense-gradient backward. Model computation, optimizer, rollout, reward, Ray and communication are excluded. A separate public pretrained Qwen3-0.6B matched generated-token update fixture (B1, prompt106+response32, BF16, TIS clamp2, SGD) measured 80.979 -> 80.454 ms with overlapping ranges and unchanged peak memory; that fixture does not establish an actor speedup. Its shared parameter gradients matched an independent FP32 score-domain oracle, while the legacy route differed by 1.37% relative L2. A second bounded B1 fixture uses prompt4064+response32, top-k32/top-p1 and an actual processed support of 32–36 tokens. It measured **126.796 -> 114.068 ms (-10.0%)** over four observations per route, with input/initial-weight-inclusive peak memory **16,957,184,000 -> 14,469,977,088 bytes (-2.316 GiB)**. Loss absolute difference was 1.99e-8 and parameter gradients were finite, but candidate-versus-legacy BF16 parameter-gradient relative L2 was **4.49%** on this very low-entropy fixture. This is one controlled unsharded update fixture, not a distributed actor or an RL-step benchmark.

A separate FP64 score-domain diagnostic on the same fixture construction explains the numerical sensitivity: shared response-logits gradients differed by 0.0263% relative L2 (max absolute 1.49e-8), versus 0.301% for the legacy path. BF16 model-parameter gradients still differed by 3.55% relative L2 from that score reference, compared with 4.69% for legacy; no exact model-gradient equivalence is claimed. The original FP32 absolute-logsumexp oracle was itself sensitive to cancellation at near-zero log-probs and is retained in the artifacts rather than treated as ground truth. A singleton-support variant correctly produces zero shared/oracle gradients and is not counted as an effective model update.

These results do not establish training quality, distributed FSDP acceptance or end-to-end RL performance.

### API and Usage Example

No new user configuration is required. SC still tries verified support alignment first and otherwise uses the configured head/trainer approximation. The FSDP engine supplies its already rolled/SP-sliced sampled labels to the SC logits processor. Callers without sampled labels retain the old correction-helper route, and hooks without shared sampled scores retain the existing CE fallback.

Manual benchmark (run on an idle CUDA device):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --active --no-sync python benchmarks/benchmark_score_centering.py --output score_centering_benchmark.json
```

### Design & Code Changes

- Share one chunked full-vocabulary forward normalizer across head/sample scoring and detached head-mass diagnostics. Complete rows normalize their loss directly over finite recorded support.
- Avoid full-vocabulary softmax recomputation in backward for complete rows; fallback rows reuse the shared normalizer. CUDA row selection has no GPU-to-host synchronization.
- Accumulate sparse head/sample collisions in FP32 before casting; retain dense vocabulary-sized logits gradients. Keep logits unchanged for entropy/KL and other graph consumers.
- Pass already local prediction labels through FSDP; gather/unpad outputs once in the packed route and preserve the existing dense route.

The full-vocabulary mass diagnostic still requires O(NV) forward work for every row. This change does not turn the model LM head or dense logits-gradient allocation into K-only work. The new helper requires a materialized full local vocabulary and must not be applied directly to an unmaterialized TP shard.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the contribution guide and repository template.
- [x] Run all pre-commit hooks and relevant CPU/CUDA tests.
- [x] Update SC cost documentation and add a manual benchmark.
- [x] New CPU/GPU regression filenames are discovered by the existing unit-test workflows.
- [x] The submitting human confirmed reviewing every changed line and independently running relevant tests.
- [x] Published and read back the exact final head; title, pre-commit, type/docstring coverage, secrets scan, CodeRabbit and CLA checks passed.
- [ ] CPU/GPU main-base workflows are not automatically triggered on this stacked base. Rebase/retarget after #8196 merges, then verify those checks on the resulting head.

AI assistance: implementation, review drafts and local validation were prepared with OpenAI Codex. The human maintainer confirmed reviewing every changed line and independently running relevant tests before publication.

+"""Manually benchmark shared score-centering normalization on an idle CUDA GPU.
+
+Run from a checkout with the FSDP CUDA dependencies installed:
+
+    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 uv run --no-sync python benchmarks/benchmark_score_centering.py \
+        --n 4096 --v 151936 --k 128 --dtype bfloat16 --warmup 4 --rounds 6 \
+        --output score_centering_benchmark.json
+
+The synthetic fixture measures score/loss forward and dense logits-gradient backward.
+It excludes model forward, optimizer, rollout, Ray, DP/SP and communication. Both routes
+retain the same head-mass and alignment diagnostics; the candidate still needs a
+full-vocabulary forward normalization for the detached trainer head-mass metric.
+The baseline is the auto-correction helper plus separately computed sampled CE.
+Timing uses identical inputs and ABBA order, after untimed numerical checks and warm-up.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+import os
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import torch
+
+
+def _source_metadata(root, sc):
+    files = {
+        "score_centering": Path(sc.__file__),
+        "shared_scores": root / "verl/trainer/ppo/score_centering_scores.py",
+        "sampled_ce": root / "verl/utils/torch_functional.py",
+        "benchmark": Path(__file__),
+    }
+    metadata = {
+        "source_sha256": {name: hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for name, path in files.items()},
+    }
+    try:
+        revision = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+        status = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+        metadata["git_head"] = revision.stdout.strip() if revision.returncode == 0 else None
+        metadata["git_dirty"] = bool(status.stdout.strip()) if status.returncode == 0 else None
+    except FileNotFoundError:
+        metadata.update(git_head=None, git_dirty=None)
+    return metadata
+
+
+def _benchmark_case(args, dtype, aligned_fraction, sc, logprobs_from_logits):
+    n, v, k = args.n, args.v, args.k
+    rule = lambda ratio: ratio.clamp(max=2.0)
+    logits = torch.randn(n, v, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    logits[:, :k] += 10.0
+    logits.requires_grad_(True)
+    ids = torch.arange(k, device="cuda").expand(n, k).contiguous()
+    aligned = torch.arange(n, device="cuda") < int(n * aligned_fraction)
+    q_head = torch.log_softmax(torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda") * 1.1, -1) + math.log(0.97)
+    support_size = max(1, 3 * k // 4)
+    support_q = q_head.masked_fill(torch.arange(k, device="cuda").unsqueeze(0) >= support_size, float("-inf"))
+    support_q = support_q - support_q.logsumexp(-1, keepdim=True)
+    q_head = torch.where(aligned.unsqueeze(-1), support_q, q_head)
+    labels = torch.where(
+        aligned,
+        torch.zeros(n, device="cuda", dtype=torch.long),
+        torch.full((n,), k + 7, device="cuda", dtype=torch.long),
+    )
+    q_sample = torch.where(aligned, q_head[:, 0], torch.full((n,), math.log(0.03 / (v - k)), device="cuda"))
+    advantages = torch.randn(n, device="cuda")
+
+    def baseline():
+        head = sc.topk_log_probs_from_logits(logits, ids)
+        correction, log_mass, q_mass, train_mass = sc.score_centering_auto_correction(head, q_head, rule, aligned)
+        sample = logprobs_from_logits(logits, labels, inplace_backward=False) - log_mass
+        tail_mass = (1 - q_mass).clamp(min=0)
+        return {
+            "sc_correction": correction,
+            "log_probs": sample,
+            "sc_train_head_mass": train_mass,
+            "sc_sampler_head_mass": q_mass,
+            "sc_log_support_mass": log_mass,
+            "sc_support_aligned": aligned.float(),
+            "sc_sampler_tail_mass": tail_mass,
+            "sc_support_unknown": ((~aligned) & (tail_mass <= 1e-6)).float(),
+        }
+
+    def run(mode):
+        logits.grad = None
+        outputs = (
+            baseline()
+            if mode == "baseline"
+            else sc.score_centering_shared_scores_from_logits(logits, ids, labels, q_head, aligned, rule)
+        )
+        lp = outputs["log_probs"]
+        weights = rule((lp.detach() - q_sample).exp())
+        loss = -(advantages * (weights * lp - outputs["sc_correction"])).mean()
+        loss.backward()
+        return loss.detach(), outputs
+
+    baseline_loss, baseline_out = run("baseline")
+    baseline_grad = logits.grad.clone()
+    candidate_loss, candidate_out = run("candidate")
+    # log_support_mass differs by contract: the candidate has already
+    # normalized sampled scores, so it returns zero for that internal field.
+    metric_names = (
+        "sc_train_head_mass",
+        "sc_sampler_head_mass",
+        "sc_support_aligned",
+        "sc_sampler_tail_mass",
+        "sc_support_unknown",
+    )
+    parity = {
+        "loss_abs_diff": (candidate_loss - baseline_loss).abs().item(),
+        "grad_max_abs_diff": (logits.grad - baseline_grad).abs().max().item(),
+        "sampled_score_max_abs_diff": (candidate_out["log_probs"] - baseline_out["log_probs"]).abs().max().item(),
+        "metric_max_abs_diff": max(
+            (candidate_out[name] - baseline_out[name]).abs().max().item() for name in metric_names
+        ),
+    }
+    del baseline_out, candidate_out, baseline_grad, baseline_loss, candidate_loss
+    for _ in range(args.warmup):
+        run("baseline")
+        run("candidate")
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    samples = {"baseline": [], "candidate": []}
+    for _ in range(args.rounds):
+        for mode in ("baseline", "candidate", "candidate", "baseline"):
+            start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record()
+            run(mode)
+            end.record()
+            end.synchronize()
+            samples[mode].append(start.elapsed_time(end))
+    timing = {
+        mode: {
+            "median_ms": statistics.median(values),
+            "min_ms": min(values),
+            "max_ms": max(values),
+            "count": len(values),
+            "samples_ms": values,
+        }
+        for mode, values in samples.items()
+    }
+    peak = {}
+    for mode in ("baseline", "candidate"):
+        logits.grad = None
+        gc.collect()
+        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
+        initial_bytes = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
+        run(mode)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        peak[mode] = {"initial_bytes": initial_bytes, "peak_bytes": torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()}
+    return {"aligned_fraction": aligned_fraction, "parity": parity, "timing": timing, "peak_allocated": peak}
+
+
+def main():
+    """Run the matched benchmark and emit its configuration, parity and cost as JSON."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    parser.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=4096, help="Number of prediction positions.")
+    parser.add_argument("--v", type=int, default=151936, help="Full local vocabulary size.")
+    parser.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=128, help="Recorded head size.")
+    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=("bfloat16", "float32"), default="bfloat16")
+    parser.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=4, help="Untimed calls per route before ABBA timing.")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--rounds", type=int, default=6, help="ABBA rounds; each route gets two observations per round."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=8196)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="Optional JSON output file; results also print to stdout.")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.n <= 0 or args.k <= 0 or args.v <= args.k + 7:
+        parser.error("Require n > 0, k > 0 and v > k + 7 for the sampled-outside-head fixture.")
+    if args.warmup < 0 or args.rounds <= 0:
+        parser.error("Require warmup >= 0 and rounds > 0.")
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        parser.error("This benchmark requires a CUDA GPU and the FSDP CUDA environment.")
+
+    # Prefer this checkout even when another verl checkout is installed editable.
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(root))
+    from verl.trainer.ppo import score_centering as sc
+    from verl.trainer.ppo import score_centering_scores as sc_scores
+    from verl.utils import torch_functional as verl_F
+
+    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
+    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(args.seed)
+    n, v, k = args.n, args.v, args.k
+    dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
+    result = {
+        **_source_metadata(root, sc),
+        "torch": torch.__version__,
+        "cuda": torch.version.cuda,
+        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
+        "dtype": args.dtype,
+        "n": n,
+        "v": v,

+def weight_fn(mode):
+    if mode == "none":
+        return torch.ones_like
+    if mode == "tis":
+        return lambda ratio: ratio.clamp(max=2.0)
+    return lambda ratio: torch.where((ratio >= 0.6) & (ratio <= 1.8), ratio, torch.zeros_like(ratio))

+def fixture(dtype=torch.float32, device="cpu"):
+    torch.manual_seed(8196)
+    n, v, k = 6, 13, 5
+    trainer_logits = (torch.randn(n, v, device=device) * 1.3).to(dtype)
+    sampler_logits = torch.randn(n, v, device=device) * 1.8
+    sizes = [2, 4, 8, 13, 5, 9]
+    order = sampler_logits.argsort(-1, descending=True)
+    keep = torch.arange(v, device=device).unsqueeze(0) < torch.tensor(sizes, device=device).unsqueeze(1)
+    sampler_logits.scatter_(1, order, sampler_logits.gather(1, order).masked_fill(~keep, float("-inf")))
+    log_q = torch.log_softmax(sampler_logits, -1)
+    ids = order[:, :k]
+    q_head = log_q.gather(-1, ids)
+    complete = torch.tensor([True, True, False, False, True, False], device=device)
+    # Rows 2/3/5 sample beyond the recorded head while staying in the true support.
+    columns = torch.tensor([0, 3, 6, 10, 4, 7], device=device)
+    labels = order.gather(-1, columns.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)

+def reference(logits, ids, labels, q_head, complete, rule):
+    """Old full-V normalized head and sampled CE, then the per-row core route."""
+    full_lp = torch.log_softmax(logits.float(), -1)
+    head = full_lp.gather(-1, ids)
+    fallback, sampler_mass, fallback_mass = score_centering_correction(head, q_head, rule)
+    aligned, log_mass, _ = score_centering_support_correction(head, q_head, rule)
+    correction = torch.where(complete, aligned, fallback)
+    log_mass = torch.where(complete, log_mass, torch.zeros_like(log_mass))
+    sampled = full_lp.gather(-1, labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1) - log_mass
+    train_mass = torch.where(complete, log_mass.detach().exp(), fallback_mass)
+    return {
+        "sc_correction": correction,
+        "log_probs": sampled,
+        "sc_sampler_head_mass": sampler_mass,
+        "sc_train_head_mass": train_mass,
+    }

+def direct_torch_oracle(logits, ids, labels, q_head, complete, rule):
+    """Small-tensor oracle only; deliberately not a performance implementation."""
+    full_lp = torch.log_softmax(logits.float(), -1)
+    raw_head = logits.gather(-1, ids).float()
+    finite = q_head.isfinite()
+    support_lse = raw_head.masked_fill(~finite, float("-inf")).logsumexp(-1)
+    support_lp = (raw_head - support_lse.unsqueeze(-1)).masked_fill(~finite, 0.0)
+    head_full_lp = full_lp.gather(-1, ids)
+    selected_lp = torch.where(complete.unsqueeze(-1), support_lp, head_full_lp)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        q = q_head.exp()
+        selected_p = selected_lp.exp() * (~complete.unsqueeze(-1) | finite)
+        ratio = torch.where(finite, (selected_lp - q_head).exp(), torch.ones_like(q))
+        weighted = q * rule(ratio)
+        p_mass, q_mass = selected_p.sum(-1), q.sum(-1)
+        rho = (1 - q_mass).clamp_min(1e-6) / (1 - p_mass).clamp_min(1e-6)
+        alpha = rho * rule(1 / rho)
+        fallback_residual = weighted - alpha.unsqueeze(-1) * selected_p
+        support_residual = weighted - weighted.sum(-1, keepdim=True) * selected_p
+        residual = torch.where(complete.unsqueeze(-1), support_residual, fallback_residual)
+    correction = (residual * selected_lp).sum(-1)
+    full_sampled = full_lp.gather(-1, labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+    support_sampled = logits.gather(-1, labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1).float() - support_lse
+    sampled = torch.where(complete, support_sampled, full_sampled)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        head_p = head_full_lp.exp()
+        train_mass = torch.where(complete, (head_p * finite).sum(-1), head_p.sum(-1))
+    return {
+        "sc_correction": correction,
+        "log_probs": sampled,
+        "sc_sampler_head_mass": q_head.exp().sum(-1),
+        "sc_train_head_mass": train_mass,
+    }
+
+
+def loss(outputs, logits, q_sampled, advantages, rule, auxiliary):
+    lp = outputs["log_probs"]
+    weights = rule((lp.detach() - q_sampled).exp())
+    result = -(advantages * (weights * lp - outputs["sc_correction"])).mean()
+    if auxiliary:
+        full_lp = torch.log_softmax(logits.float(), -1)
+        entropy = -(full_lp.exp() * full_lp).sum(-1).mean()
+        # Preserve current KL consumer semantics; reference LP remains a fixed scalar.
+        diff = -2.0 - lp
+        kl = (diff.exp() - 1 - diff).mean()
+        result = result - 0.02 * entropy + 0.01 * kl
+    return result
+

+"""Shared head/sample scoring for FSDP's full local vocabulary.

+This is a separate backend path: the general auto-correction helper continues to

+

+        logits,
+        gradient,
+        maxima,
+        denominators,
+        coefficients,
+        aligned,
+        vocab: tl.constexpr,
+        logits_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+        logits_col_stride: tl.constexpr,
+        grad_row_stride: tl.constexpr,
+        grad_col_stride: tl.constexpr,
+        block: tl.constexpr,
+    ):
+        row = tl.program_id(0)
+        columns = tl.program_id(1) * block + tl.arange(0, block)
+        in_vocab = columns < vocab
+        if tl.load(aligned + row):
+            values = tl.full((block,), 0.0, tl.float32)
+        else:
+            values = tl.load(
+                logits + row * logits_row_stride + columns * logits_col_stride,
+                mask=in_vocab,
+                other=-float("inf"),
+            ).to(tl.float32)
+            maximum = tl.load(maxima + row)
+            denominator = tl.load(denominators + row)
+            coefficient = tl.load(coefficients + row)
+            values = -coefficient * tl.exp(values - maximum) / denominator
+        tl.store(gradient + row * grad_row_stride + columns * grad_col_stride, values, mask=in_vocab)

+class _SharedScoreCenteringScores(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, logits, head_ids, labels, sampler_head, aligned, weight_fn, chunk_size):
+        n = logits.shape[0]
+        chunk_size = chunk_size if chunk_size > 0 else max(n, 1)
+        correction = torch.empty(n, device=logits.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+        sampled = torch.empty_like(correction)
+        train_mass = torch.empty_like(correction)
+        maxima = torch.empty_like(correction)
+        denominators = torch.empty_like(correction)
+        residuals = torch.empty(head_ids.shape, device=logits.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+        head_probabilities = torch.empty_like(residuals)

+            end = min(start + chunk_size, n)

+            raw_head = work.gather(-1, head_ids[start:end])

+            maximum = work.max(-1).values
+            work.sub_(maximum.unsqueeze(-1)).exp_()
+            denominator = work.sum(-1)

+            q_lp = sampler_head[start:end].float()

+    @staticmethod
+    @torch.autograd.function.once_differentiable

+        if grad_sampled is None:

+        grad_sampled = grad_sampled.float()
+        coefficients = grad_head.sum(-1) + grad_sampled

+        )
+        grad_input = torch.empty_like(logits)

+                grad_input,
+                maxima,
+                denominators,
+                coefficients,
+                aligned,
+                vocab,
+                logits.stride(0),
+                logits.stride(1),
+                grad_input.stride(0),
+                grad_input.stride(1),
+                block,
+                num_warps=4,
+            )
+        else:
+            grad_input.zero_()

+                end = min(start + ctx.chunk_size, n)
+                rows = (~aligned[start:end]).nonzero().squeeze(-1) + start
+                work = logits.index_select(0, rows).to(dtype=torch.float32, copy=True)
+                work.sub_(maxima[rows].unsqueeze(-1)).exp_().div_(denominators[rows].unsqueeze(-1))
+                work.mul_(-coefficients[rows].unsqueeze(-1))
+                grad_input.index_copy_(0, rows, work.to(logits.dtype))
+        # Reduce duplicate head/sample ids within the small K+1 matrix. Then
+        # overwrite their dense gradient entries after one fp32 accumulation,
+        # without allocating a full-vocabulary fp32 gradient workspace.
+        sparse_ids = torch.cat((ids, labels.unsqueeze(-1)), dim=-1)
+        sparse_values = torch.cat((grad_head, grad_sampled.unsqueeze(-1)), dim=-1)
+        sorted_ids, order = sparse_ids.sort(-1)
+        sorted_values = sparse_values.gather(-1, order)
+        starts = torch.ones_like(sorted_ids, dtype=torch.bool)
+        starts[:, 1:] = sorted_ids[:, 1:] != sorted_ids[:, :-1]
+        groups = starts.long().cumsum(-1) - 1
+        compact_ids = torch.zeros_like(sorted_ids).scatter_(-1, groups, sorted_ids)
+        compact_values = torch.zeros_like(sorted_values).scatter_add_(-1, groups, sorted_values)
+        valid = torch.arange(sparse_ids.shape[-1], device=logits.device).unsqueeze(0) < starts.sum(-1, keepdim=True)
+        # Unused slots repeat the first group's exact id/value, so repeated
+        # stores write an identical result rather than overwriting a live id.
+        compact_ids = torch.where(valid, compact_ids, compact_ids[:, :1])
+        compact_values = torch.where(valid, compact_values, compact_values[:, :1])
+        base = logits.gather(-1, compact_ids).float()
+        base.sub_(maxima.unsqueeze(-1)).exp_().div_(denominators.unsqueeze(-1))
+        base.mul_(-coefficients.unsqueeze(-1))
+        base = torch.where(aligned.unsqueeze(-1), torch.zeros_like(base), base)
+        grad_input.scatter_(-1, compact_ids, (base + compact_values).to(logits.dtype))
+        return grad_input, None, None, None, None, None, None

+def score_centering_shared_scores_from_logits(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    head_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    sampled_token_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    sampler_head_log_probs: torch.Tensor,
+    support_complete: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_fn: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],

+        sampled_token_ids.long(),
